answer: Each seat is one licensed timber scaler carrying a state-stamped brand die and an assigned sale. When the seed names a meadow landing and a delta float, that scaler brands every butt log, tags it, and files a tally of species, diameter and board feet. The mill re-measures each tag at intake; a line off by five percent voids the load. Scalers sharing a die or a cut block fold into one vote and forfeit 60,000 POA. Licence, surety and travel run $2,400 a seat, so a thousand clones need a thousand hands in a thousand walnut stands. A brand burns into sapwood; a copied die leaves soot.
